# Disclaimer and Development Process Disclosure

---

## Summary

This is an **experimental research project**. It has **not been audited**, it is **not finished**,
and it must **not be used with real funds** — you can lose assets at any stage.

**Heavy LLM usage.** Most of the design documents, code, tests and documentation were generated by
large language models and reviewed by a human. Generated code can contain mistakes. Testing has so
far found 11 bugs in LLM-generated code here, including three memory-safety issues (dangling
references to values that had gone out of scope) and one case where the reference implementation
used as a test oracle was itself wrong.

Because of that, **passing tests is not treated as proof of safety** in this project. Unverified
areas are stated as unverified. See the bug log in
[firmware/tests/README.md](firmware/tests/README.md).

**What this means for you**

- Do not store real funds. Do not use it for anything you cannot afford to lose.
- Verify everything on test networks first (Bitcoin Signet / Ethereum Sepolia).
- Read the source, run the tests, and please report what you find.

---

- **Last updated**: 2026-10-12
- **Target version**: v0.1 (in development)

## 0. Bottom line first

> **This is an experimental project. It is under development. Do not deposit real cryptocurrency funds into it.**
>
> **Development makes heavy use of LLMs (large language models). Generated code can contain mistakes.**
>

## 1. It is experimental and in development

This project (zhww) is an **experimental research and development project**, not a finished product.

| Item | Current state |
|---|---|
| Status | **experimental / work in progress**. Specifications, APIs and file layout change without notice |
| Implemented scope | BIP39 / BIP32 / Base58 / Bech32 / Bech32m / RIPEMD-160 / BTC address generation, PSBT parsing and signing (single-signature, 2-of-3 multisig, Taproot), EVM signing (EIP-155 / EIP-1559 / EIP-191 / EIP-712), ABI decoding, ERC-7730 clear signing, BC-UR transport, FAT32 (microSD exchange), and a host-side screen UI. **Bitcoin Core accepts the signatures this code produces.** |
| **Not implemented** | **on-device screen output, camera hardware support, and any run on real hardware. The firmware has never executed on the target board.** The screen UI exists only as a host-side preview, and the QR decoder (implemented and verified on the host against independent encoders) has never been fed a real camera image. |
| Tests | 304 tests pass against official test vectors. But "the tests passed" ≠ "it is safe" |
| Audit | **Not performed. None scheduled either** |
| Track record | **No** record of signing or sending on real hardware |

**In other words, at this point it cannot be used as a hardware wallet.** It is currently at the stage of "verifying the parts list, the architecture and the cryptographic primitives".

## 2. Disclosure of LLM (large language model) usage

### 2.1 Development setup

**Most** of this project's design, implementation, tests and documentation **is generated by LLMs**.

| Role | Owner |
|---|---|
| Design decisions, requirements, acceptance of deliverables | **Human** |
| Design documents, code, tests, documentation | **LLM** (coding agents) |
| Security judgements (threat model, documenting residual risk) | Human (a human reviews the LLM's proposals) |
| Verification (running tests, cross-checking against official vectors) | Automated tests + human review |

Concretely, the Zig implementation (`firmware/src/`), the tests (`firmware/tests/`) and
the design documents in `docs/` are generated by LLMs and then reviewed and corrected
by a human.

### 2.2 Concrete risks of using LLMs

"Cryptocurrency code written by an LLM" has to be handled more carefully than ordinary software.

| Risk | Description | Mitigation in this project |
|---|---|---|
| **Hallucination** | Using APIs that do not exist, describing plausible but wrong specifications | Cross-checking against official test vectors. Mechanical verification by the compiler and the tests |
| **Subtle cryptographic bugs** | Runs without raising any error, but derives a wrong key for rare inputs | Explicit tests of boundary conditions (asymmetric inputs, depth, block boundaries) |
| **Oversights** | Errors remain in areas the tests do not verify | Anything not covered by tests is treated as "unverified" |
| **Overconfidence** | Mistaking "the tests passed" for "it is safe" | Stated repeatedly in this file and the README |
| **Gaps in the security design** | Missing pieces in the threat model (side channels, physical attacks, etc.) | Residual risks are listed as "what we cannot protect" in [docs/05-threat-model.md](docs/05-threat-model.md) |

### 2.3 Bugs actually found in LLM-generated code (record)

The tests have actually detected errors in LLM-generated code.

| Bug detected | Description |
|---|---|
| Byte order reversed | BIP39 entropy extraction was reversed. It did not show up in the official vectors where the same byte repeats, such as `7f7f7f...` |
| Derivation from the wrong depth | Passing the absolute path `m/0'/1` to a non-master key descended one level too many. Fixed by forbidding it in the API |

The details are recorded in [firmware/tests/README.md](firmware/tests/README.md).
**Both of these are the kind of bug that would have stayed in the code if the tests had not existed.** Assume that bugs of the same kind may still be present.

### 2.4 It is not "dangerous because it uses an LLM" but "dangerous because it is not verified"

It is not the use of LLMs itself but the **degree of verification** that determines safety.
This project emphasises the following kinds of verification.

1. Agreement with **official test vectors** (BIP39 / BIP32 / BIP49 / BIP84 / BIP86)
2. Cross-checking against **external implementations** (Bitcoin Core, viem / ethers.js, etc.) — to be added
3. **Preventing misuse through the API** (e.g. rejecting absolute paths on anything but a master key)
4. **Reviews are welcome** — we welcome reports via issues and pull requests

---

## 3. Uses that are not allowed

**Avoid the following outright.**

- **Storing real funds** (it is not finished as a hardware wallet yet)
- **Managing large amounts with a single signature**
- **Embedding this repository's code as-is into a product or service**
- **Distributing it to others while describing it as "safe"**
- **Generating a seed (mnemonic) with only this project's unverified code, without backing it up by other means**

---

## 4. If you really must try it

Understanding that you do so at your own risk, at a minimum follow the rules below.

1. **Verify the whole flow on test networks** (Bitcoin Signet / Ethereum Sepolia)
2. **Start with small amounts**
3. Use a **multisig setup** so that one faulty or leaky device cannot lose everything
4. **Always back up the mnemonic by hand** (a metal plate is recommended)
5. **Build releases yourself and verify the hash**
6. **Power the device off when you are done** (this design keeps the seed in RAM only)

## 6. Reporting vulnerabilities

If you find a security problem, please do not open a public issue; contact us first through GitHub
Security Advisories (a private report).
Even if a fix is difficult, **letting us know helps protect users**.

> In place: `SECURITY.md` (the vulnerability disclosure policy).
